input.content:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, statsmodels.api as sm
from cyvcf2 import VCF
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
D="/analysis-001/data/inputs/f-geno/"
NPC=10; MAF_MIN=0.01; CALL_MIN=0.95
ph=pd.read_csv(D+"pheno.txt",sep="\t")
v=VCF(D+"cohort.vcf.gz"); samples=list(v.samples)
meta=[];G=[]
for r in v:
    gt=np.array(r.genotypes)[:,:2]
    g=np.where((gt<0).any(1),np.nan,gt.sum(1)).astype(float)
    meta.append((r.ID,r.CHROM,r.POS,r.REF,r.ALT[0],r.FILTER or "PASS"));G.append(g)
G=np.array(G).T  # samples x variants
meta=pd.DataFrame(meta,columns=["rsid","chromosome","position","ref","alt","filter"])
ph=ph.set_index("IID").loc[samples]; y=ph.PHENO1.values.astype(float)
print("pheno NaN",np.isnan(y).sum())
cr=1-np.isnan(G).mean(0); af=np.nanmean(G,0)/2; maf=np.minimum(af,1-af)
keep=(cr>=CALL_MIN)&(maf>=MAF_MIN)
print("variants kept",keep.sum(),"of",len(keep))
# PCA on standardized, mean-imputed genotypes
Gi=np.where(np.isnan(G),np.nanmean(G,0),G)
Z=(Gi[:,keep]-Gi[:,keep].mean(0))/Gi[:,keep].std(0)
U,S,Vt=np.linalg.svd(Z,full_matrices=False)
pcs=U[:,:NPC]*S[:NPC]
# relatedness check
K=Z@Z.T/Z.shape[1]; np.fill_diagonal(K,0)
print("max off-diag GRM",K.max(),"pairs>0.177:",(np.triu(K)>0.177).sum())
pd.DataFrame(pcs,index=samples,columns=[f"PC{i+1}" for i in range(NPC)]).to_csv("output/pcs.csv")
rows=[]
C=sm.add_constant(pcs)
for j in np.where(keep)[0]:
    X=np.column_stack([Gi[:,j],C]); m=sm.OLS(y,X).fit()
    rows.append((j,m.params[0],m.bse[0],m.pvalues[0]))
res=pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=["j","beta","standard_error","pvalue"]).set_index("j")
out=meta.loc[res.index].join(res); out["maf"]=maf[res.index]; out["effect_allele"]=out.alt
out=out.drop(columns="filter").sort_values("pvalue"); out.to_csv("output/gwas_results.csv",index=False)
p=out.pvalue.values; lam=np.median(stats.chi2.isf(p,1))/stats.chi2.ppf(.5,1)
print("lambda_GC",lam)
# unadjusted lambda for comparison
p0=[sm.OLS(y,sm.add_constant(Gi[:,j])).fit().pvalues[1] for j in np.where(keep)[0]]
lam0=np.median(stats.chi2.isf(p0,1))/stats.chi2.ppf(.5,1); print("lambda unadjusted",lam0)
pd.DataFrame({"lambda_gc_adjusted":[lam],"lambda_gc_unadjusted":[lam0],"n_variants":[len(out)],"n_samples":[len(y)]}).to_csv("output/lambda.csv",index=False)
# QQ
ps=np.sort(p); n=len(ps); exp=-np.log10((np.arange(1,n+1)-.5)/n); obs=-np.log10(ps)
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(5,5))
ax.scatter(exp,obs,s=8,color="#31688e"); ax.plot([0,exp.max()],[0,exp.max()],"k--",lw=1,label="expected")
ax.set(xlabel="Expected -log10(p)",ylabel="Observed -log10(p)",title="QQ plot: LDL cholesterol (adj. 10 PCs)")
ax.text(.05,.9,f"λGC = {lam:.3f}\nN = {len(y)}, variants = {n}",transform=ax.transAxes); ax.legend(loc="lower right")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("figures/qq_plot.png",dpi=300); fig.savefig("figures/qq_plot.pdf")
# Manhattan
o=out.copy(); o["c"]=o.chromosome.str.replace("chr","").astype(int); o=o.sort_values(["c","position"])
off=0;xs=[];tk=[]
for c,d in o.groupby("c"):
    xs.append(d.position+off); tk.append((off+d.position.mean(),c)); off+=d.position.max()+1e7
o["x"]=pd.concat(xs)
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(10,4))
ax.scatter(o.x,-np.log10(o.pvalue),s=6,c=np.where(o.c%2,"#440154","#35b779"))
ax.axhline(-np.log10(5e-8),color="k",ls="--",lw=1); ax.axhline(5,color="gray",ls=":",lw=1)
ax.set_xticks([t[0] for t in tk]); ax.set_xticklabels([t[1] for t in tk],fontsize=7)
ax.set(xlabel="Chromosome",ylabel="-log10(p)",title="LDL cholesterol GWAS"); fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("figures/manhattan.png",dpi=300); fig.savefig("figures/manhattan.pdf")
print(out.head(15).to_string())
print("p<5e-8:",(p<5e-8).sum(),"p<1e-5:",(p<1e-5).sum())

results.text:
Two variants reach genome-wide significance (p < 5e-8) for LDL cholesterol after adjusting for 10 principal components. Population structure had to be corrected first: without adjustment λGC was 3.75, and with 10 PCs it is 1.013.

I used 600 samples and 3,000 PASS variants. None were dropped by the filters (call rate ≥95%, MAF ≥1%). The model is linear regression of LDL on additive genotype dosage plus the 10 PCs. PLINK2 is not installed, so I ran the association in Python with cyvcf2 and statsmodels. The maximum pairwise relatedness was 0.109, below the 0.177 first-degree-relative cutoff, so no samples were removed.

| Variant | Position (GRCh38) | Effect (beta, mg/dL per G allele) | SE | p-value | MAF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rs100900 | chr21:9,975,700 | +13.4 | 1.59 | 2.5e-16 | 0.43 |
| rs100100 | chr13:1,997,300 | +12.7 | 2.02 | 7.4e-10 | 0.195 |
| rs102500 | chr15:25,932,500 | +10.0 | 2.08 | 1.7e-6 | 0.19 |

- **rs102500** is only suggestive (p < 1e-5), not genome-wide significant. Nothing else gets below p = 4.5e-5 (rs101694), and all variants are in the results file.
- **QQ plot:** the points follow the diagonal except for the top hits, which is consistent with the λGC of 1.013.
- **Caveats:** with only 600 samples and 3,000 variants this is a small, sparse panel. The loci are not annotated to genes because no annotation resource was used. Effect sizes for the top hits may be inflated, and none is replicated. A larger cohort and fine-mapping would be needed before treating these as causal.

Files are in `/analysis-001/runs/run-001/T1S1`:
- output/gwas_results.csv
- output/lambda.csv
- output/pcs.csv
- figures/qq_plot.png and figures/qq_plot.pdf
- figures/manhattan.png and figures/manhattan.pdf
- scripts/gwas.py
